title: Total vs Partial Ordering
goal: Distinguish strict total orderings from partial orderings.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Morning: Standard Traits

sections.text: In Java or C++, primitive numeric comparisons assume all values can be ordered. Rust distinguishes total orderings from partial orderings.

sections.caption: Floats implement `PartialOrd` because NaN cannot be ordered.

sections.text: Because `f64::NAN > 0.0` and `f64::NAN <= 0.0` are both false, floating point types cannot implement `Ord`.
The `partial_cmp` method returns `Option<Ordering>`, where unordered values return `None`.

sections.caption: `partial_cmp` returns `None` when comparing against NaN.

sections.text: Types with full total order implement `Ord`, which is required by key-based structures like `BTreeMap`.

explanation: Distinguish strict total orderings from partial orderings.
